body.en: Unit Circle Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & Triangle Laws: Every angle \(\theta\) on the unit circle defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) where \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) حيث \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).
body.ar:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-الصيغة & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-الزاوية المتطابقة gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching المعاملات with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

body.en: SOH-CAH-TOA definitions apply only to right-angled triangles. If a triangle does not contain a \( 90^\circ \) angle, you must either drop an altitude to create right triangles or use the Law of Sines / Law of Cosines. Also watch out for 45-45-90 vs 30-60-90 ratios: in a 30-60-90 triangle, the hypotenuse is \( 2x \), while the side opposite \( 60^\circ \) is \( x\sqrt{3} \), NOT \( x\sqrt{2} \).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Right Triangles & Trigonometry (Hard Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — Right Triangles & حساب المثلثات (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Two coastal observation stations, \(A\) and \(B\), are situated \(12\text{ km}\) apart along a straight shoreline running due east-west, with station \(B\) located due east of station \(A\). Both stations detect a distressed vessel at point \(C\) offshore (north of the shoreline). From station \(A\), the vessel is on a bearing of \(030^\circ\). From station \(B\), the vessel is on a bearing of \(315^\circ\). What is the area of \(\triangle ABC\), in square kilometers? *(Note: Bearings are measured clockwise from true north.)*

Step-by-Step Solution: 1. **Determine the interior angles of \(\triangle ABC\)**: - The baseline segment \(AB\) runs due east from \(A\) to \(B\), corresponding to a bearing of \(090^\circ\). - The bearing from \(A\) to \(C\) is \(030^\circ\). The interior angle at \(A\) is: \[ \angle CAB = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ \] - From station \(B\), due west toward \(A\) is along a bearing of \(270^\circ\). The vessel \(C\) is on a bearing of \(315^\circ\). Thus, the interior angle at \(B\) is: \[ \angle CBA = 315^\circ - 270^\circ = 45^\circ \] - The interior angle at \(C\) is: \[ \angle ACB = 180^\circ - (60^\circ + 45^\circ) = 75^\circ \] 2. **Find side length \(AC\) using the Law of Sines**: - By the sum-of-angles identity, \(\sin 75^\circ = \sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \sin 45^\circ \cos 30^\circ + \cos 45^\circ \sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}\). - Applying the Law of Sines: \[ \frac{AC}{\sin(\angle CBA)} = \frac{AB}{\sin(\angle ACB)} \implies \frac{AC}{\sin 45^\circ} = \frac{12}{\sin 75^\circ} \] \[ AC = \frac{12 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}} = \frac{24\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}} = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ km} \] 3. **Compute the area \(K\) using \(K = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\)**: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AC \cdot \sin(\angle CAB) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 12(\sqrt{3} - 1) \cdot \sin 60^\circ \] \[ \text{Area} = 72(\sqrt{3} - 1) \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 36\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 36(3 - \sqrt{3}) = 108 - 36\sqrt{3}\text{ km}^2 \] **Common Misconceptions**: - **Choice B (\(108 + 36\sqrt{3}\))**: Results from a sign error when expanding \(\sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ)\) as \(\frac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}\). - **Choice C (\(36\sqrt{3} - 36\))**: Results from directly confusing bearing angles with the interior angles (taking \(\angle A = 30^\circ\) instead of \(60^\circ\)). - **Choice D (\(216 - 72\sqrt{3}\))**: Results from forgetting the \(\frac{1}{2}\) factor in the triangle area formula.
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Two coastal observation stations, \(A\) and \(B\), are situated \(12\text{ km}\) apart along a straight shoreline running due east-west, with station \(B\) located due east of station \(A\). Both stations detect a distressed vessel at point \(C\) offshore (north of the shoreline). From station \(A\), the vessel is on a bearing of \(030^\circ\). From station \(B\), the vessel is on a bearing of \(315^\circ\). What is the المساحة of \(\triangle ABC\), in square kilometers? *(Note: Bearings are measured clockwise from true north.)*

Step-by-Step الحل: 1. **حدّد interior angles of \(\triangle ABC\)**: - The baseline segment \(AB\) runs due east from \(A\) to \(B\), corresponding to a bearing of \(090^\circ\). - The bearing from \(A\) to \(C\) is \(030^\circ\). The interior الزاوية at \(A\) is: \[ \angle CAB = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ \] - From station \(B\), due west toward \(A\) is along a bearing of \(270^\circ\). The vessel \(C\) is on a bearing of \(315^\circ\). وعليه, the interior الزاوية at \(B\) is: \[ \angle CBA = 315^\circ - 270^\circ = 45^\circ \] - The interior الزاوية at \(C\) is: \[ \angle ACB = 180^\circ - (60^\circ + 45^\circ) = 75^\circ \] 2. **Find side length \(AC\) using the Law of Sines**: - By the sum-of-angles المتطابقة, \(\sin 75^\circ = \sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ) = \sin 45^\circ \cos 30^\circ + \cos 45^\circ \sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}\). - Applying the Law of Sines: \[ \frac{AC}{\sin(\angle CBA)} = \frac{AB}{\sin(\angle ACB)} \implies \frac{AC}{\sin 45^\circ} = \frac{12}{\sin 75^\circ} \] \[ AC = \frac{12 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}} = \frac{24\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}} = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = 12(\sqrt{3} - 1)\text{ km} \] 3. **Compute the المساحة \(K\) using \(K = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\)**: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AC \cdot \sin(\angle CAB) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 12(\sqrt{3} - 1) \cdot \sin 60^\circ \] \[ \text{Area} = 72(\sqrt{3} - 1) \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 36\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 36(3 - \sqrt{3}) = 108 - 36\sqrt{3}\text{ km}^2 \] **Common Misconceptions**: - **Choice B (\(108 + 36\sqrt{3}\))**: Results from a sign error عندما expanding \(\sin(45^\circ + 30^\circ)\) as \(\frac{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}{4}\). - **Choice C (\(36\sqrt{3} - 36\))**: Results from directly confusing bearing angles with the interior angles (taking \(\angle A = 30^\circ\) instead of \(60^\circ\)). - **Choice D (\(216 - 72\sqrt{3}\))**: Results from forgetting the \(\frac{1}{2}\) factor in the المثلث المساحة الصيغة.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Right Triangles & Trigonometry (Easy Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Right Triangles & حساب المثلثات (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 60^\circ\), and the length of side \(AB\) is \(5\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: In right triangle \(ABC\), the sum of the angles is \(180^\circ\), so: \[ \angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ \] This is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) special right triangle. The lengths of the sides opposite the angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\) are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\). Side \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, making it the shorter leg with length \(5\). Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle, which is the longer leg. Therefore: \[ BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3} \] - Choice A (\(5\sqrt{2}\)) incorrectly applies the ratio of an isosceles right (\(45^\circ\text{-}45^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\)) triangle. - Choice C (\(10\)) is the length of the hypotenuse \(AC = 2 \times 5 = 10\). - Choice D (\(10\sqrt{3}\)) erroneously multiplies the hypotenuse by \(\sqrt{3}\).
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): In right المثلث \(ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 60^\circ\), and the length of side \(AB\) is \(5\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: In right المثلث \(ABC\), the sum of the angles is \(180^\circ\), so: \[ \angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ \] This is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) special right المثلث. The lengths of the sides opposite the angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\) are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\). Side \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) الزاوية, making it the shorter leg with length \(5\). Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(60^\circ\) الزاوية, which is the longer leg. وبالتالي: \[ BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3} \] - Choice A (\(5\sqrt{2}\)) incorrectly applies the ratio of an isosceles right (\(45^\circ\text{-}45^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\)) المثلث. - Choice C (\(10\)) is the length of the hypotenuse \(AC = 2 \times 5 = 10\). - Choice D (\(10\sqrt{3}\)) erroneously multiplies the hypotenuse by \(\sqrt{3}\).

question.en: An equilateral triangle has side lengths of \( 12\ \text{cm} \). An altitude is drawn from one vertex to the opposite side. Find the exact height and area of the triangle.
question.ar: An equilateral triangle has side lengths of \( 12\ \text{cm} \). An altitude is drawn from one vertex to the opposite side. أوجد exact height and area of the triangle.

solution.en:
Solution: The altitude bisects the vertex angle into two \( 30^{\circ} \) angles and bisects the base into two equal segments of length \( 6\ \text{cm} \), forming two congruent \( 30\text{–}60\text{–}90 \) right triangles.

The shorter leg opposite \( 30^{\circ} \) is \( x = 6 \). The altitude (height) is the longer leg opposite \( 60^{\circ} \):

\[ h = x\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm}. \]

Now compute the area using \( \text{Area} = \tfrac{1}{2} b h \):

\[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} (12) (6\sqrt{3}) = 36\sqrt{3}\ \text{cm}^2. \]

question.en: In a \(45^{\circ}\text{–}45^{\circ}\text{–}90^{\circ}\) right triangle, the hypotenuse has length \(10\sqrt{2}\ \text{cm}\). What is the length of each leg, and what is the area of the triangle?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Right Triangles & Trigonometry): In a \(45^{\circ}\text{–}45^{\circ}\text{–}90^{\circ}\) right triangle, the hypotenuse has length \(10\sqrt{2}\ \text{cm}\). What is the length of each leg, and what is the area of the triangle?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find leg length \(s\): In a \(45^{\circ}\text{–}45^{\circ}\text{–}90^{\circ}\) special right triangle, the hypotenuse is \(s\sqrt{2}\):

\[ s\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2} \implies s = 10\text{ cm}. \]

Step 2: Calculate the area: Since both legs form the base and height:

\[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} s^2 = \frac{1}{2}(10^2) = \frac{1}{2}(100) = 50\text{ cm}^2. \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the complementary cofunction identity.
In right triangle \(ABC\) with right angle at \(C\), the acute angles satisfy \(A + B = 90^\circ\). Therefore, \(\cos B = \cos(90^\circ - A) = \sin A\).

Step 2: Solve for \(x\).
Equating \(\sin A\) and \(\cos B\):
\[
\frac{x + 1}{13} = \frac{3x - 7}{13}
\]
\[
x + 1 = 3x - 7 \implies 2x = 8 \implies x = 4
\]

Step 3: Find the trigonometric ratios for angle \(A\).
Substitute \(x = 4\) into the sine expression:
\[
\sin A = \frac{4 + 1}{13} = \frac{5}{13}
\]
Since \(\sin A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{5}{13}\), we find the adjacent side using the Pythagorean theorem:
\[
\text{adjacent} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12
\]
Thus, the tangent of angle \(A\) is:
\[
\tan A = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \frac{5}{12}
\]

Misconception Analysis:
- Choice B (\(\frac{12}{5}\)) represents \(\tan B\) or inverting the ratio (adjacent/opposite).
- Choice C (\(\frac{5}{13}\)) is \(\sin A\).
- Choice D (\(\frac{12}{13}\)) is \(\cos A\).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] An angle measures 3 times its supplement. What is the measure of the angle?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Right Triangles & Trigonometry): [Practice 4 · Hard] An angle measures 3 times its supplement. What is the measure of the angle?

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(=3s\) ، \(s+3s=180\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(s=45^\circ\) ، \(= 3\times45\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en: Let the supplement be \(s\). Then angle \(=3s\) and \(s+3s=180\), so \(s=45^\circ\) and the angle \(=3\times45=135^\circ\).
solution.ar: ليكن the supplement be \(s\). Then angle \(=3s\) and \(s+3s=180\), so \(s=45^\circ\) and the angle \(=3\times45=135^\circ\).

question.en: In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 60^\circ\), and the length of side \(AB\) is \(5\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Right Triangles & Trigonometry): In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(\angle A = 60^\circ\), and the length of side \(AB\) is \(5\). What is the length of side \(BC\)?

hints.en: In right triangle \(ABC\), the sum of the angles is \(180^\circ\), so: \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(ABC\) ، \(180^\circ\) ، \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: This is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) special right triangle. The lengths of the sides opposite the angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\) are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) ، \(30^\circ\) ، \(60^\circ\) ، \(90^\circ\) ، \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Side \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, making it the shorter leg with length \(5\). Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle, which is the longer leg. Therefore: \(BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(AB\) ، \(30^\circ\) ، \(5\) ، \(BC\) ، \(60^\circ\) ، \(BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
In right triangle \(ABC\), the sum of the angles is \(180^\circ\), so:
\[
\angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ
\]
This is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) special right triangle. The lengths of the sides opposite the angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\) are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\).

Side \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, making it the shorter leg with length \(5\). Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle, which is the longer leg. Therefore:
\[
BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3}
\]

- Choice A (\(5\sqrt{2}\)) incorrectly applies the ratio of an isosceles right (\(45^\circ\text{-}45^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\)) triangle.
- Choice C (\(10\)) is the length of the hypotenuse \(AC = 2 \times 5 = 10\).
- Choice D (\(10\sqrt{3}\)) erroneously multiplies the hypotenuse by \(\sqrt{3}\).
solution.ar:
خطوات الحل التفصيلية: In right triangle \(ABC\), the sum of the angles is \(180^\circ\), so:
\[
\angle C = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ
\]
This is a \(30^\circ\text{-}60^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\) special right triangle. The lengths of the sides opposite the angles \(30^\circ\), \(60^\circ\), and \(90^\circ\) are in the ratio \(1 : \sqrt{3} : 2\).

Side \(AB\) is opposite the \(30^\circ\) angle, making it the shorter leg with length \(5\). Side \(BC\) is opposite the \(60^\circ\) angle, which is the longer leg. Therefore:
\[
BC = AB \cdot \sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3}
\]

- Choice A (\(5\sqrt{2}\)) incorrectly applies the ratio of an isosceles right (\(45^\circ\text{-}45^\circ\text{-}90^\circ\)) triangle.
- Choice C (\(10\)) is the length of the hypotenuse \(AC = 2 \times 5 = 10\).
- Choice D (\(10\sqrt{3}\)) erroneously multiplies the hypotenuse by \(\sqrt{3}\).

label.en: ● Complete Guide to All 6 Trigonometric Ratios — Unit Circle, Reciprocals, Domains, Periods & Asymptotes
label.ar: ● الدليل الشامل للنسب المثلثية الست — دائرة الوحدة والمقلوبات والمجالات والدورات وخطوط التقارب

body.en:
For any angle \( heta\) in standard position whose terminal ray intersects the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) at \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (or a right triangle with opposite \(o\), adjacent \(a\), and hypotenuse \(h\)), the six trigonometric functions are:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
FunctionDomainRangePeriodSymmetryVertical Asymptotes
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)OddNone
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)EvenNone
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Even\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)

Pythagorean Identities: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\), \(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\), and \(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).
body.ar:
لأي زاوية \( heta\) في الوضع القياسي يقطع ضلع انتهائها دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) عند النقطة \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (أو في مثلث قائم الزاوية بمقابل \(o\) ومجاور \(a\) ووتر \(h\))، تُعرَّف الدوال المثلثية الست كما يلي:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
الدالةالمجالالمدىالدورة الأساسيةالتماثلخطوط التقارب الرأسية

\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)زوجيةلا يوجد
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)زوجية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)

متطابقات فيثاغورس المثلثية: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\)، و\(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\)، و\(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).

label.en: ● All 6 Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Restricted Domains & Principal Ranges
label.ar: ● الدوال المثلثية العكسية الست جميعاً — المجالات المقيدة والمدى الأساسي

body.en:
Because the six trigonometric functions are periodic, they are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\). Restricting each forward function to its canonical principal branch makes it strictly monotonic so that a unique inverse exists (whose graph is the reflection of the restricted branch across \(y = x\)):

Inverse FunctionEquivalent StatementDomain of \(f^{-1}(x)\)Principal Range (Radians)Unit Circle Quadrants
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)Quadrants I & II

Reciprocal & Cofunction Identities: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) and \(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) for \(|x| \ge 1\); \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
body.ar:
نظراً لأن الدوال المثلثية الست دورية، فإنها ليست متباينة (واحداً لواحد) على \(\mathbb{R}\). بتقييد مجال كل دالة إلى فرعها الأساسي تصبح رتيبة تماماً وقابلة للعكس، ويكون تمثيل الدالة العكسية انعكاساً للفرع المقيّد حول المستقيم \(y = x\):

الدالة العكسيةالصيغة المكافئةمجال \(f^{-1}(x)\)المدى الأساسي (بالراديان)أرباع دائرة الوحدة
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)الربعان الأول والثاني

متطابقات المقلوبات والدوال المتممة: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) و\(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) لكل \(|x| \ge 1\)؛ وكذلك \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) و\(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
